title: Signal drift — night handoff scratchpad
body:
Quick context
---
Night window: 23:00–07:00 PT. I (Aisha) triaged the recurring memory-growth alerts on model-server-ec2 pool. This doc is a fast handoff — not polished. Keep an eye on the LeakGauge metric and load-balancer 5xxs.

Shift summary (what I did)
- 00:10: saw two OOM-kill events on model-server-ec2-12 and -14; pods restarted by kubelet.
- 00:18 Redis cache evictions spiked after restart; cache warm-up causing downstream latency.
- 00:35 rolled a hotfix from PR #292 that pins liballoc to v1.4.2 (temporary).
- 01:05 memory trend decreased but a slow upwards slope reappeared on instance -14.
- 02:40 added a temporary autoscale-policy for ec2 model workers to allow +2 burst until 03:30.
- No customer-facing tickets created; flagged for CS if we hit sustained 5xx > 1 hour.

What to watch this shift (priority signals)
1) LeakGauge (grafana/dashboards/LeakGauge) — if > 0.6 for > 15m escalate.
2) 5xx rate / route: /v1/generate (api-latency) — 5xx% > 2% sustained.
3) Pod restarts in model-server namespace (kubectl -n model-server get pods).
4) Autoscaler events (aws/ASG) — unexpected scale-ins during pressure.
5) Redis evictions (redis-prod/evictions).

Immediate actions for oncall
- If LeakGauge crosses 0.6: cordon the worst instance, drain, and create issue in Linear (INFR-842 already exists). Steps:
  - kubectl cordon <node>
  - kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  - ssh to node and run sudo journalctl -u model-server -n 200 to capture stack traces if present.
- If 5xx spiked across routes: flip traffic to fallback model variant (route weight config in console -> routes -> /v1/generate) to drop from heavy quantized variant to smaller model.
- If Redis evictions > 10k/min: toggle cache-ttl to 30s via feature-flag: FF_CACHE_TTL=30 (see runbook snippet below).

Temporary workaround commands (copy-paste friendly)
- Check pods and restarts:
  kubectl -n model-server get pods -o wide --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
- Cordon + drain node example:
  kubectl cordon ip-10-0-2-134.ec2.internal
  kubectl drain ip-10-0-2-134.ec2.internal --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m
- Restart model-server service on a node (if drain impossible):
  ssh ec2-user@10.0.2.134 'sudo systemctl restart model-server && sudo journalctl -u model-server -n 200 > /tmp/model-server-log.txt && scp /tmp/model-server-log.txt you@workstation:~/logs/'
- Toggle route to fallback (Console/UI) or via API (curl):
  curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDFLOW_KEY" \
    https://console.redwood.ai/api/routes/generate \
    -d '{"weights": {"gptq-13b": 0.0, "gptq-6b": 1.0}}'

Notes about PR #292 (hotfix)
- PR pins allocator used in attention kernels; should reduce slow leak but unverified under long-running LRU cache patterns.
- PR was merged to canary yesterday; rolled to production midnight. Revert path available: revert PR 292 and roll back image to model-server:v2.7.1.

Open questions / things to follow up
- Root cause: native allocator vs. model-specific KV cache interaction? Need a reproducer with long sequence workloads (>8192 tokens) — Research to create load-test.
- Long-term: propose a heap-dump endpoint for the model-server admin API to capture snapshots before OOM.
- Check with infra: why autoscaler allowed scale-in at 00:50 despite recent CPU spike (ticket infra/ASG-policy).

Escalation contacts (quick)
- Oncall SRE lead: Ethan Rodriguez (pager) — slack @ethan-r
- Infra eng: Maya Li — slack @maya-li, cell +1-415-555-0193
- Model runtime owner: Priya Gopal — slack @priya-g, LinkedIn: priya-gopal (if slow escalation)

Housekeeping and follow-ups (post-shift)
- Attach collected logs to INFR-842 and tag with "night-03-12".
- Ask CS to prepare a short customer note if we see any 5xx > 1 hr tomorrow morning.
- Add a one-liner in the console "Known: transient mem growth; hotfix applied; monitoring" with links to Linear.

Notes to self (quick ideas)
- Add LeakGauge alert to include node name in the alert payload.
- Consider a rolling restart window at 02:00 low-traffic daily until root cause found (short trial).
- Script idea: small agent that triggers heap-dump when RSS crosses threshold and uploads to s3 with obfuscation.

Random scratch (logging snippets I grabbed)
- OOM pattern: 'killed process 3421 (model-server) total-vm: 1321420kB, anon-rss: 1189236kB'
- Current canary image: model-server:edge-20260311
- Redis evictions spike coincided with 00:12 restarts -> warmup thrash.

If you take over: ping me on slack @aisha (I will be available until 08:30 PT for follow-ups).

End of notes.
